plain: A state of unrest or stirred-up feeling

webster.text: A gentle boiling; or the internal motion of the constituent parts of a fluid.

more.text: Intestine motion; heat; tumult; agitation; as, to put the passions in a ferment; the state or people are in a ferment.

example.quote: So far otherwise, that the Hatter’s Act was never regarded; the act to destroy the Land Bank scheme raised a greater ferment in this province than the Stamp Act did, which was appeased only by passing province laws directly in opposition to it.
